summary.text: Cynthia (Cinde) Wirth is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 6th Congressional District. A Columbus, Indiana native, she has worked as a high school science teacher, small business owner, researcher, and federal legislative fellow. She was the Democratic nominee in 2024 and says she is running on health care, education and affordability.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Columbus, Indiana; graduated from Columbus North High School. She describes herself as a first-generation college graduate.

Earned a B.A. in biology and Spanish from the University of Evansville (1992), an M.A. in anthropology/archaeology/underwater cultural resource management from Indiana University Bloomington (2009), and a Ph.D. from Ball State University (2025).

Worked as a high school biology and environmental science teacher, a research consultant, and a facilitator of biology and environmental science with CSA New Tech, and has been a small business owner.

Was selected as an Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellow with the U.S. Department of Energy as a legislative fellow, and her campaign website says one of the federal bills she wrote there became law in 2020.
Has served as an Educational Ambassador for Friends of Miyoshi, Japan, and her Ballotpedia profile lists professional affiliations including archaeology societies and Sunrise Rotary.
Ran for the seat in 2024 as the Democratic nominee and lost the general election to Jefferson Shreve, 31.7% to 63.9%.
According to her campaign materials, she and her husband, Trent, have lived in downtown Columbus for 30 years and have two grown children.
